title: Decision process, budget and RouteWise
gist: CFO Dana Whitfield signs off after a pilot on Harbor & Pine's own trucks, with a decision by Oct 30; budget is around $300k/yr if the numbers hold, and RouteWise is competing at about $52 per truck per month.

turns.t: So let me switch gears a little. Marcus, if this goes well, how does a decision actually get made at Harbor & Pine? Who else needs to be involved?

So, I own operations. I'm the one who's going to live with it and I'm the one pushing for it. But anything at this size goes to Dana. Dana Whitfield, our CFO. She signs off, and honestly she's the one I have to convince. She's not anti, she's just, she's been burned. We bought a yard management thing two years ago that was supposed to save us a fortune, and we turned it off after eight months. She brings it up. Not often. But she brings it up.
Got it. What would Dana need to see?

Numbers on our trucks. Not your case study, not a nice slide about some grocery fleet in Ohio. She'll want a pilot. We want a pilot, frankly. Run it on a chunk of the fleet, show me the miles, show me overtime, show me late deliveries on those routes, and then we talk.
That makes total sense. And timing, is there a date you're working toward?

October 30th. We want a decision by the end of October. Dana does the budget for next year in November, and if it's not in by then, it's basically next fiscal year, and I really don't want to go through another peak like this one.
Okay, October 30. That's tight with a pilot in there, but doable if we move this week.
It's tight, I know. I'd rather it be tight.

Just thinking out loud. If the decision is October 30, the pilot can't be a full quarter. We'd need something that shows real signal in, what, four weeks? Can you get Dana a read on overtime in four weeks?

Overtime, yes, that's weekly payroll, it shows up fast. Chargebacks lag. They come in thirty to forty-five days after the delivery. So we'd see overtime and on-time pretty quick, and then chargebacks we'd have to kind of project.
Okay, that's useful. On-time at the DC appointment is a pretty good leading indicator for chargebacks. We could make that the headline metric and project the dollars off it.
And budget, I'll just ask directly. Is there budget set aside for this, or is this something that has to be carved out?

So, I'll be candid. I've got a number in my head and I've talked to Dana about the range. Something in the neighborhood of three hundred k a year is, um, it's not crazy to us. If the numbers hold. If you come in and the pilot shows we save half the overtime and half the chargebacks, that's well over three hundred, and it's an easy conversation. If the pilot's mushy, three hundred k is a very hard conversation and I'm the guy who brought it in.
That's fair, and honestly that's the right way to buy this. For context, at 420 trucks we'd land right around there, a little over at list, depending on terms.
Yeah. And look, I'll be straight with you about the other thing too, since you're going to ask anyway. We're talking to RouteWise.
Sure. I figured you might be.
Their number came in around fifty-two dollars a truck a month. So, that's cheaper. Noticeably cheaper.
Yeah. What do you like about them so far, other than that?

Price. Honestly, it's mostly price. The demo was fine. It felt a bit, like, older? The dispatch screen looked like our spreadsheets with a nicer font. But they did say they have an Oracle connector, which got Elena's attention.
It got my attention. It did not get my trust. I asked if it was certified for our version and they said they would follow up. That was two weeks ago.

Got it. Look, I won't trash them, they're a real company and they've got customers. What I'd say is, the price per truck isn't the number Dana's going to care about. It's what the routes save. Our beta fleets on the new engine, Routing v3, are seeing about eleven percent fewer miles driven, and on-time going from ninety-one to almost ninety-five percent. If that holds on your fleet, a few dollars a truck is kind of a rounding error.
If it holds. Everybody's beta is great.

That's fair. That's exactly what the pilot's for. But let me just do the napkin math out loud, and correct me where I'm off. Forty k a month in chargebacks is call it four hundred and eighty k a year. If we take half of that, that's two-forty. Then overtime. I don't know your payroll, but if you've got, what, four-hundred-some drivers and fourteen percent of their hours are at time and a half, going from fourteen to eight is a big number. Probably bigger than the chargebacks. So against three hundred k, the math works pretty fast, even if we only hit half of what you said good looks like.
Yeah. I've done that napkin too. It's why I'm on this call. But Dana doesn't buy napkins. She buys the spreadsheet with our payroll in it.

Totally. And that's the one we'll build together, with your numbers. I'm just saying the gap between us and RouteWise is about sixteen bucks a truck, and the thing you're trying to fix is a lot bigger than sixteen bucks a truck.

Ha. Okay. I'll give you that one. For now. So, the criteria. I'll tell you how I'd frame it for Dana. One, does it actually cut overtime and late deliveries on our trucks. Two, can Elena integrate it without a six-month project. Three, does it pass security. And four, price. Price is fourth, but it's on the list, I'm not going to pretend it isn't.
That's super helpful. Elena, would you add anything?
Only that the integration is a gate, not a score. If it doesn't work with the TMS, it does not matter how good the routes are.
Understood. Gate, not a score. I'll use that. And on the paper side, once Dana says yes, what does that look like? Legal, procurement, anything we should know about?

So, we don't have a procurement team, really. It's me, Dana, and our outside counsel looks at the MSA. They're not slow, but they're not free either, so Dana likes it when vendors use reasonable paper. Last time it took about two weeks from yes to signature. And Elena's security sign-off has to be done before legal will even open it.
That's correct. Security first, then legal. Not in parallel. I've asked.
Okay, that's important. So if we're working back from October 30, security review has to basically be done by the time the pilot's wrapping up. Which means the questionnaire needs to start this week.
Yeah. That's the critical path, honestly. Not the pilot.
And for the pilot itself, I'm thinking out loud, but would you want it on one terminal or spread across all three? Like, a chunk of Kent?

Kent, probably. It's the biggest, it's got the worst chargeback accounts, and Ray's there, so if it works there it works anywhere. Fifty, sixty trucks maybe. I don't want to bet the whole terminal on a pilot in peak. Dana would kill me.

Fifty or sixty trucks in Kent. That's a really sensible size. Let me take that back and we'll put together something concrete on what a pilot looks like, including how we'd measure it, so Dana's not looking at our numbers, she's looking at yours.
That would help a lot. If the measurement is my payroll data and my on-time data, she'll trust it. If it's your dashboard she'll assume it's marketing.

title: Live ETA sharing and next steps
gist: Marcus calls live ETA sharing a must-have; Tom says it is on the roadmap for this quarter while Asher hedges that it is still being scoped. The group books a Routing v3 demo with Daniel for Thursday Oct 1 and agrees on security, data and briefing follow-ups.

turns.t: Okay. Can I get on my soapbox now?
Please. The customer calls.

The customer calls. So, our retail customers, and some of the industrial ones too, they keep calling dispatchers asking where's my truck. All day. My dispatchers, the same people who are supposed to be fixing the plan when something breaks, spend I'd say a third of their day on the phone telling a receiving manager at a DC that the truck is twenty minutes out. And half the time they're guessing, because they're looking at a dot on the Samsara map and doing math in their head. So what I really want is something where the customer gets a link, they see the truck, they see a real ETA, and they stop calling us. Is that something you do? Live ETA sharing, tracking link, whatever you call it.
Yeah, so, that's on the roadmap for this quarter. It's something we're actively working on, and honestly it's one of the things I'm most excited about, because we hear it from a lot of fleets.
This quarter, like, by the end of the year?
That's the plan, yeah.

Yeah, I, um. Just to be precise about where it is. We're scoping it now. The ETA piece underneath it is real, it's the same model that's in the new routing engine, and it's gotten a lot more accurate this year. But the customer-facing link itself, I don't want to give you a date on this call and then have to walk it back in three weeks. Let me come back to you with something firmer.

Okay. I appreciate that. I'm just going to be honest, that one's a must-have for us. Not a nice-to-have. If I go to Dana and say we cut overtime but the dispatchers are still on the phone all day, half the value is gone. And the customers who call the most are the same ones charging us back.
Totally hear you. And it's the right priority. We'll make sure you have a clear picture of it well before the pilot decision.
And if it exists, it has to work off the Samsara GPS, not some separate app on the driver's phone. We are not putting another app on 420 phones. The drivers already hate the one they have.
Yep, understood. That's a really good constraint to know now.

And just so you know the size of it. I had one of my leads tally calls for a week in August. Kent alone, about three hundred and forty inbound where's-my-truck calls. In a week. That's one terminal. So it's not a little feature for us. It's probably a full dispatcher's worth of time, maybe two.
That's a great stat. Can I use that with our product team? It really helps make the case internally.
Use it. Please. Make the case. I'd rather you build it than RouteWise does.
That's really helpful, genuinely. That kind of number moves things up a list. I'll take it back.
Okay. Good.

So, next steps. Here's what I'd propose. Thursday, October 1st, we do a real demo. I'll bring Daniel, our staff engineer. He'll show you Routing v3, the dispatch board, re-planning when a truck goes down, and he can go deep with Elena on Samsara and the TMS question. Does Thursday work?
Thursday. What time are you thinking?
How about eleven Pacific? I'll book forty-five minutes in case Elena has a lot of questions.
I will have a lot of questions.
Eleven works. I'll move a thing.

Great. On my side, I'll send the SOC 2 report under NDA today or tomorrow. Elena, if you can send over the security questionnaire, I'll get our team started on it right away. And I'll find out about Oracle on-prem references.
I'll send the questionnaire after this call. And the TMS version details and a sample of the nightly export, so Daniel can look at it before Thursday.
Perfect, that'd be really helpful.
And Marcus, if you could share one night's routes, even just one terminal, anonymized is fine, we can run it through the engine before Thursday so the demo's on your network and not some fake city.
Oh, that'd be great actually. I can get you Kent from last Tuesday. That was a bad night, so it's a good test.
Even better. And Marcus, is it worth looping Dana in at any point before the pilot? Even fifteen minutes?
Not yet. Let me brief her after Thursday. If I bring her in too early she'll ask for the ROI model and we don't have it yet. Once I've seen the demo I'll know what I'm actually pitching.

Makes sense. Okay, let me just recap so we're all on the same page, and then I'll let you go. Thursday at eleven Pacific, Routing v3 demo with Daniel, ideally on your Kent data from last Tuesday. Before that, I send the SOC 2 report under NDA, Elena sends the questionnaire, the TMS version and a sample export, and I come back on Oracle on-prem references. After Thursday, Marcus briefs Dana, and we put together a pilot proposal, fifty to sixty trucks in Kent, measured on your payroll and on-time data, so you can make a decision by October 30. And on live ETA, we owe you something firmer. Did I miss anything?
SCIM. Asher said he'd confirm.
Yes, SCIM. On me.
Perfect. Thank you both, this was really, really useful.
Yeah, thanks guys. Good call.
Thank you. Talk Thursday.
Thanks, see you Thursday.
